s: John the Baptist prepares the way. Jesus is baptized, calls disciples and heals many in Galilee.
Jesus forgives and heals a paralysed man, calls Levi, and is Lord of the sabbath.
Jesus chooses the twelve. His family thinks he is out of his mind. Whoever does God's will is my brother and sister and mother.
Parables of the sower and the mustard seed. Jesus calms the storm.
Jesus frees a man possessed by a legion of demons, heals a woman who touches his cloak and raises Jairus's daughter.
Jesus is rejected at Nazareth and sends out the twelve. John the Baptist is killed. Jesus feeds five thousand and walks on water.
What comes out of a person defiles him. Jesus heals the daughter of a Syrophoenician woman and a deaf man.
Jesus feeds four thousand. Peter confesses him as the Christ, and Jesus foretells his passion: take up your cross.
The Transfiguration. Jesus heals a possessed boy and teaches the disciples to be servants of all.
Jesus teaches on marriage and blesses children. The rich man goes away sad. Blind Bartimaeus receives his sight.
Jesus enters Jerusalem, curses a fig tree and cleanses the temple.
The wicked tenants. Render to Caesar. The greatest commandment. A poor widow gives all she has.
Jesus foretells the temple's destruction and tells his disciples to watch.
Jesus is anointed at Bethany. The Last Supper, the agony in the garden, the arrest, and Peter's denial.
Jesus is condemned by Pilate, crucified and buried. The centurion says: truly this man was the Son of God.
The women find the tomb empty. The risen Jesus appears and sends the disciples to preach to the whole world, and ascends to heaven.

1: At the Jordan the Spirit comes down on Jesus and the Father calls him his beloved Son. Jesus' public ministry begins.
14: On the night before he dies, Jesus gives his body and blood to his disciples. This is the beginning of the Eucharist.
15: Jesus dies on the cross, and a Roman centurion confesses that he is the Son of God.
16: The women find the tomb empty, and an angel tells them Jesus is risen.

“My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”

Jesus is not saying that God has abandoned him. These are the opening words of [[Psalm 22|psalms/22/2]]. In ancient Jewish teaching and oral tradition, standard practice called for referencing an entire Psalm by invoking its first line. Reciting the opening line was intended to direct listeners to the full text and context of the passage. In that Psalm, there’s a mocking crowd, the pierced hands and feet, the soldiers casting lots for his garments. Jesus is showing that the Scripture is being fulfilled in him. Psalm 22 does not end in despair. It transitions from anguish to praise, ending with God delivering the sufferer and establishing his kingdom across all nations.
